key_insight: PsychFound is a psychiatry-specialized LLM fine-tuned on expert guidelines and de-identified clinical records that achieves clinical‑grade performance and measurably improves diagnostic and treatment decisions when integrated into psychiatric workflows.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between general-purpose LLMs and the specific, high-stakes needs of psychiatric clinical practice by providing reliable, domain-adapted decision support acceptable to clinicians.
method: Curated multi-source training: combine psychiatry expert knowledge, guideline text, and de-identified electronic health records for domain adaptation.
Instruction-tuning and evaluation: fine-tune with clinician-authored prompts and validate against clinical benchmarks and prospective workflow trials.
Safety and deployment controls: calibration of uncertainty, human-in-the-loop review, and alignment checks to reduce hallucination and risk in clinical use.
impact: Demonstrates that targeted domain-adaptation + rigorous clinical evaluation can produce LLMs suitable for real-world medical workflows, providing a reproducible template for ML practitioners building high‑stakes, domain-specific assistants.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data sources (guidelines, EHRs, experts) → fine-tuning → clinical integration
Bar chart: performance comparison (PsychFound vs. general LLMs) across diagnostic accuracy, treatment recommendation quality, and safety metrics
Clinical workflow schematic: clinician + PsychFound interactions showing human-in-loop checkpoints
Safety & evaluation checklist iconography: calibration, uncertainty flags, audit trail
paper_title: A domain-adapted large language model to support clinicians in psychiatric clinical practice
paper_authors: Ruoxi Wang, Shuyu Liu, Ling Zhang, Xuequan Zhu, Zhi Yang
